slides.title: ekam
slides.subtitle: all in one - one question, one verified answer, one place. सब एक जगह।
slides.notes: ekam means 'one' in Sanskrit. Introduce it as a verified-opportunity finder: you ask in your own words, and you get one clean, source-linked answer instead of a tab graveyard.

slides.title: One question in India costs thirty tabs
slides.body: A job, a flat, a tender, a scheme: the answer exists, but it is scattered across dozens of sites full of duplicate, stale and fake listings.
slides.notes: Anchor the pain: nothing here is a data-availability problem, it is a trust and fragmentation problem. A student in Meerut and a founder in Coimbatore ask the same question in different words and both end up with noise.

slides.title: Stale, fake and duplicated listings are the norm

stats.label: of users hit the same broken search

slides.notes: Be explicit with judges: these are problem descriptors, not traction numbers. The point is that duplication, staleness and missing provenance are structural, and no vertical-specific job board fixes them.

slides.title: ekam verifies the answer before it shows you
slides.body: Ask in plain English or Hindi - typed or spoken - and get one clean, source-linked dataset you can trust and export.
slides.notes: The wedge: ekam is not another aggregator. Every row carries its source and timestamp, so 'verified' is checkable, not a claim. No source, no row.

slides.title: Every question runs one verified pipeline
slides.notes: Walk the live pipeline users see in the workspace: interpret, fetch, verify. Highlight verify - that is the differentiator. Gemini handles interpretation with a deterministic regex fallback, so the product works even when the model doesn't.

slides.title: From landing to export in three moves

items.title: Get Started
items.body: One unified button opens the sign-in / sign-up overlay.

items.title: One onboarding question
items.body: What will you use ekam for? The workspace adapts.

items.title: Ask, watch, export
items.body: Live pipeline, verified results, CSV/JSON export.

slides.notes: This flow is shipped. Four signup paths - job seeker, student, SME/founder, agency - shape the workspace, not just a label. Emphasise there are no forms, no filters, no boolean syntax anywhere.

items.title: Voice input, shipped

items.title: Ask anything

items.body: Asking twice shows one entry, not ten.

slides.notes: Four product principles that separate ekam from a vertical job board. Voice is not a dictation toy - it is the primary interface for users whose first language is not English.

slides.title: Ask it the way you'd say it
slides.body: "mujhe Noida mein flat dikhao" and "AI developer jobs in Bengaluru" both land in the same pipeline - intent, vertical and location extracted from one sentence.

slides.notes: Position against incumbent aggregators and vertical boards. The table is the investment thesis in miniature: provenance, dedup, bilingual, multi-vertical and data portability are design decisions, not features on a backlog.

slides.title: Ask one place, or keep opening tabs
slides.notes: Close the loop with the opening problem: the thirty-tab search collapses into one verified answer. Restate the tagline - one question, one verified answer, one place.
